newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES MIXED ON WEDNESDAY.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES MIXED ON WEDNESDAY.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted mixed in fairly quiet trade on Wednesday.
"It's a little bit confusing at the moment. The treasury bill auction rate went up but I'm not sure whether it's an indication that the market is short," one money dealer commented.

He said the central Reserve Bank came into the market on Wednesday to sell Z$500 million worth of treasury bills to discount houses but only Z$210 million was picked up at 18.11 percent, up from 17.15 percent on Tuesday.
Treasury bills were being sold on the secondary market at 17 percent while call money was unchanged at 17 percent.

Bankers acceptance bills were quoted at 18.25 percent from 17.25 (buying) and at 17.50 percent from 17.15 (selling) with 30-, 60- and 90-day NCDs buying steadily at 18 percent while their selling rate firmed to 17.75 from 16.75 percent.
Reserve Bank figures showed the market closed on Tuesday with a surplus of Z$127 million compared with Z$178 million the previous day.
